item.research_question: What is the magnetic state that develops in the highly structurally and chemically inhomogeneous Al28Co20Cr11Fe15Ni26 single-crystalline high-entropy alloy?
item.processing_route: Czochralski monocrystal growth from a heterogeneous tungsten seed under 650 mbar Ar atmosphere at a pulling rate of 1 mm/h
item.test_conditions: Direct-current magnetization, hysteresis curves, alternating-current magnetic susceptibility, and thermoremanent magnetization time decay measured from 1.8 to 400 K; magnetic fields up to 7 T and 100 mT; AC frequencies 1–1000 Hz
key_findings: The material consists of a B2 matrix (94 vol%) and spherical A2 nanoparticles (6 vol%) with an average diameter of 64 nm.
The Cr-free B2 matrix (Al28Co25Fe15Ni32) forms a disordered ferromagnetic state with a Curie temperature TC ≈ 390 K.
The A2 nanoparticles (Co19Cr56Fe25) exhibit a core-shell structure with CoFe-enriched shells of ~2 nm thickness.
The nanoparticle shells are ferromagnetic, while the nanoparticle cores are asperomagnetic (a subclass of spin glasses).
Asperomagnetism in the nanoparticle cores develops below a spin-freezing temperature Tf ≈ 15 K.
Below 15 K, the system exhibits broken-ergodicity phenomena, including a growing difference between zero-field-cooled and field-cooled magnetizations.
The low-temperature M(H) curve at 1.8 K shows a linear tail at high fields, confirming a minor antiferromagnetic component from the asperomagnetic cores.
No mictomagnetic (cluster glass) state was observed, as zfc and fc hysteresis curves perfectly overlapped at 6 K.
item.mechanism: The B2 matrix contains only ferromagnetic elements (Co, Fe, Ni) leading to a disordered ferromagnetic state with positive exchange interactions. The A2 nanoparticles contain the antiferromagnetic element Cr alongside Co and Fe, creating mixed FM/AFM interactions. This results in a distribution of exchange interactions where FM interactions dominate but AFM interactions exist, forming an asperomagnetic state in the cores. The core-shell structure arises from CoFe enrichment at the A2–B2 interfaces. The asperomagnetic state is magnetically frustrated, leading to ergodicity breaking and spin freezing below 15 K.
item.limitations: The ferromagnetic nature of the nanoparticle shells could not be verified experimentally by bulk magnetization measurements because their signal is masked by the much stronger ferromagnetic contribution from the B2 matrix.
quotes: The results reveal that the Cr-free B2 matrix of composition Al28Co25Fe15Ni32 forms a disordered ferromagnetic (FM) state that undergoes an FM transition at TC≈ 390 K.
While the shells are FM, the nanoparticle cores are asperomagnetic, classifying into the broad class of spin glasses.
Asperomagnetism develops below 15 K and exhibits broken-ergodicity phenomena, typical of magnetically frustrated systems.
